problem: Traditional navigation depends on absolute coordinate systems, precise maps and GPS, which fail in GPS-denied (underwater/underground), unexplored, and task-oriented settings where no specific route exists.
motivation: New applications need navigation without prebuilt maps or global localization. Advances in IoT and AI let a moving agent interact with the physical world to build local maps, localize objects and optimize routes, so a systematic review of this emerging embodied navigation paradigm is needed.
key_idea: Survey that frames embodied navigation as a new paradigm in which the agent interacts with the environment to obtain local maps, localization and routes, organized around perception, navigation and efficiency optimization.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation or method analysis can be reported. The abstract indicates the review is organized around perception, navigation and efficiency optimization, plus emerging tasks and real-world deployment challenges.
method: Perception: reviews how the agent perceives the environment to build local maps and localize objects
Navigation: reviews embodied navigation methods and paradigms
Efficiency optimization: reviews route and system efficiency optimization
Emerging tasks: examines new tasks enabled by flexible mobility in diverse, evolving environments
Real-world deployment: identifies challenges and extensions to broader areas
results: This is a survey with no experimental results reported in the abstract. It provides a systematic review of embodied navigation across perception, navigation, efficiency optimization, emerging tasks and real-world challenges.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so details of coverage and taxonomy cannot be assessed
As a survey, it presents no new method or benchmark results
